Captured live, never authored: these are the bytes the boot harness (`mame_machine.MACHINE_LUA`,
through MAME's `-autoboot_script`) wrote into the session's scratch on a real machine.
Program and board names were then replaced by neutral labels by a single mechanical substitution
that preserves every field width; nothing else was edited.

m68k-dual.txt   the m68k-dual board: TWO MC68000 with
               distinct tags, which is the multi-cpu case the single-cpu assumption elsewhere
               in this server would have got wrong. It carries the shapes the parser has to
               tell apart: an entry that names a REGION with its offset, one that names a
               SHARE, one that names NEITHER (a handler keeping its values off the bus), an
               entry with a MIRROR, and a `cpu_space` beside a `program` space on each cpu.
               The same bytes came back from the console route at the park, which is the
               measurement that decided the harness owns the live half.
               Every CPU line carries the device's shortname as `type=`, every SPACE line
               that space's address mask, and a REGS line per cpu the names of its state
               entries, which its console symbol table takes as its
               registers: re-captured once the gather wrote each. All four read ffffff on this board, so the case
               that tells one cpu's mask from another's derives a variant by REPLACING the
               sub cpu's program mask, and says so.

A change in MAME's Lua output is RE-CAPTURED here, never patched in the fixture: a fixture
edited by hand stops being evidence about the thing it is supposed to describe.

Captured from MAME's own `-listxml`, each run against the build that carries the set, in the
exact form the server runs it (`<binary> <system> -listxml`), stdout verbatim:

listxml-m68k-dual.xml  the m68k-dual build (`<binary> <set> -listxml`): the MULTI-CPU case
                      again, from the other source, with both 68000s' clocks; a screen with its
                      rotation; and the board's ROM files, of which the undumped ones carry
                      NO crc and NO sha1 at all, which is the absent-field case the parser
                      must not fill in.
listxml-v30.xml    the v30 build (`<binary> <set> -listxml`): a SINGLE V30 at a
                      different clock, so a reading that hard-wired two cpus or one clock is
                      red against it.

BOTH documents carry more than one <machine>: the set asked for, plus one per DEVICE the
board is built from, which on a real board is most of the document. The parser is scoped to the
set's own element for that reason. On neither of these builds does a device machine carry a chip, a rom or a display
of its own, so that exclusion has no case to be proven red against on this host.

ONE FILE HERE IS NOT A CAPTURE, and it says so on the line above the part that is not:

listxml-device-with-hardware.xml   listxml-m68k-dual.xml with THREE lines added by hand, inside
                                   the `ramdac` device machine: a marker comment, a
                                   `<chip type="cpu">` and a `<rom>`. Everything else is the
                                   capture, byte for byte.

                                   It exists because neither MAME build on the machine this was
                                   written on has a device machine carrying hardware of its own,
                                   so the half of the scoping that EXCLUDES another machine's
                                   chips had nothing to be proved red against. The shape it
                                   adds is one MAME's own DTD declares, not one invented for
                                   the test; what it is NOT is evidence about this board, and
                                   no test may read it as such. Its only job is to be excluded.
